fit_line: A builder role to "design, build and maintain AI-powered systems" with Claude Code, and the three first projects (ticket triage, lead sourcing bot, call intelligence) map closely onto Hussain's public agent repos.
ai_in_job: "You'll work hands-on with Claude Code and Grok (xAI) to turn manual workflows into reliable automations, connect them to our tools (Go High Level & Monday.com)" — AI coding agents and LLM APIs are the core of the role.

screening_answers.question: Why this role and Vroom Media Group?
screening_answers.answer: The role is what I already build: AI agents and automations for business operations, using Claude Code every day. Your three first projects (support ticketing, a lead sourcing bot, call intelligence) are close to things I have shipped publicly: ai-lead-receptionist, lead-intel-engine and multi-agent-research-crew. I also like that the process ends with a paid, real project, because that is the best way to show how I work.

screening_answers.question: Describe your hands-on experience with Claude Code and the Grok (xAI) API. Please show real projects.
screening_answers.answer: Claude Code: I use it daily to ship, and I hold the Claude Code in Action and Claude Code 101 certifications, plus CCDV-F and CCAO-F from Anthropic. Real projects: github.com/huss2003/multi-agent-research-crew (planner, researcher, writer and verifier agents on a DAG orchestrator with retries, timeouts, token budgets and claim-level citation checks), github.com/huss2003/ai-lead-receptionist (Claude agent over SMS and web chat with Twilio, qualifies leads and books jobs) and github.com/huss2003/lead-intel-engine. Grok: I have not used the xAI API in a project yet. I work with the Claude API daily and I am happy to build a Grok-backed variant of a ticket-triage flow to show you.

screening_answers.question: Tell us about an AI agent or multi-step workflow you built.
screening_answers.answer: multi-agent-research-crew: a planner splits a question, researchers run in parallel, a writer drafts and a verifier checks each claim against its citation. The orchestrator is a custom Python asyncio DAG with retries, timeouts and token budgets, so a failed step does not break the run. The same reliability thinking applies to a support-ticket triage or call-summary workflow. Code: github.com/huss2003/multi-agent-research-crew

screening_answers.question: Do you have experience integrating with CRMs or work management platforms (Monday.com, Go High Level)?
screening_answers.answer: I built a CRM at a US-based medical-device company, where I worked for 3 years as a Full Stack Developer, and built internal AI agents there. In my own projects I integrated HubSpot (PageForge) and send HMAC-signed CRM events from my portfolio backend. I have not used Monday.com or Go High Level yet. Both are API and webhook driven, which I work with regularly, and I would pick them up quickly.

screening_answers.answer: [CONFIRM: can you sustain the overnight IST schedule? Answer plainly yes or no.] Draft if yes: Yes. I am based in Pune (IST) and can work 9am–5pm Eastern, Monday to Friday.

screening_answers.answer: I am based in Pune, India, and work fully remote. I am comfortable working with a distributed team and documenting what I build so others can use it daily.
